summary: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException while tesselating block model Game crashes when breaking a block
description: The game crashed as I break a full block of oak wood slabs causing me to crash. 19w38a : [ crash-2019-09-18_21.01.43-client.txt] Description: Tesselating block model java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 1, Size: 1 at java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:653) at java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:429) at cxj.b(SourceFile:91) at cxe.a(SourceFile:306) at dps.a(SourceFile:134) at dps.b(SourceFile:76) at dps.a(SourceFile:47) at dpq.a(SourceFile:48) at dpd.a(SourceFile:1300) at dpa.a(SourceFile:691) at dpa.a(SourceFile:535) at daj.e(SourceFile:931) at daj.b(SourceFile:564) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 19w38a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place an oak wood slab on the ground.
4. Break the placed oak wood slab using any tool or directly by hand.
5. Observe that the game crashes when breaking the block.
Observed Behavior: The game crashes when attempting to break a full block of oak wood slabs in version 19w38a. The crash occurs specifically during the tessellation process of the block model, leading to a `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 1, Size: 1` error. This exception is triggered at `java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:653)` and subsequently propagates through various Minecraft classes involved in rendering and breaking blocks. The crash log indicates that the issue arises when the game tries to access an index out of bounds within an ArrayList used during block tessellation, causing the client to terminate abruptly upon attempting to break the oak wood slab. This behavior is consistent and reproducible with the same block type under the specified version.
Expected Behavior: When breaking a full block of oak wood slabs, the game should not crash. The block should be removed normally without any exceptions or errors, and the player should continue playing without interruption. The tessellation process for rendering the block model should handle all cases correctly, avoiding any out-of-bound index issues.
